platonic-solids.label: Solid: 1 tetra · 2 cube · 3 octa · 4 dodeca · 5 icosa
platonic-solids.description: Discrete solid choice: 1 tetrahedron, 2 cube, 3 octahedron, 4 dodecahedron, 5 icosahedron. The receiving module checks its own domain.

platonic-solids.label: Face count F
platonic-solids.description: A Platonic solid is a convex polyhedron with congruent regular polygon faces and the same number of faces meeting at each vertex. These five models have vertex count V, edge count E and face count F satisfying V−E+F=2. Choosing a new solid changes actual connections and counts; a projected edge crossing is not an extra vertex.

tessellation.label: Regular tile sides n
tessellation.description: Whole number of sides of each regular convex tile. The receiving module checks its own domain.

tessellation.label: Corners at one vertex q
tessellation.description: Whole number of tile corners brought to the same vertex. The receiving module checks its own domain.

tessellation.label: Signed gap angle g
tessellation.description: At a regular convex n-gon corner, the interior angle is α=180(n−2)/n degrees. Bringing q such corners together leaves signed gap g=360−qα degrees. Positive gap leaves uncovered angle and negative gap means angle overlap. The tested regular plane tilings use six triangles, four squares or three hexagons at every vertex. A local angle equation alone is not a general tiling theorem.

perspective-projection.label: Marker depth z
perspective-projection.description: Positive marker depth from the pinhole, in metres. The receiving module checks its own domain.

perspective-projection.label: Real marker width W
perspective-projection.description: Real width of the centered marker, in metres. The receiving module checks its own domain.

perspective-projection.label: Virtual image-plane distance f
perspective-projection.description: Distance to the virtual image plane, in metres. The receiving module checks its own domain.

perspective-projection.label: Image width w
perspective-projection.description: In an ideal pinhole camera, a point at sideways coordinate X and positive depth z maps to virtual-image coordinate x=fX/z. A centered marker of real width W therefore has image width w=fW/z. Magnification m=f/z is dimensionless. Real dimensions remain fixed when depth changes; the changing projection is a measured image length rather than a shrinking object.

sphere-packing.label: Packing: 1 simple cubic · 2 face-centered cubic
sphere-packing.description: Discrete packing choice: 1 simple cubic or 2 face-centered cubic. The receiving module checks its own domain.

sphere-packing.label: Sphere radius r
sphere-packing.description: Common sphere radius, in centimetres. The receiving module checks its own domain.

sphere-packing.label: Occupied volume fraction η
sphere-packing.description: A periodic packing repeats a cell whose boundary spheres are shared with neighboring cells. Simple cubic packing has eight corner eighths, totaling one sphere, and cell edge a=2r. Face-centered cubic packing adds six face halves, totaling four spheres, with face-diagonal contacts giving a=2√2r. Dividing occupied sphere volume by cube volume gives packing fraction η, which is independent of radius within each packing.
